attrs.evidence: lowering.mjs 0.2.0 freezes INPUT_PORT_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, inputsSemId, portSemId and INSTANTIATION_RECEIPT_FIELDS, with instantiate() throwing instantiate-not-implemented. LOWERING_SEM_ID MOVED as a consequence and that is the point: LOWERING_SPEC carries inputs_model, so deciding the model changes the lowering relation, and an id that survived the ruling unchanged would be claiming the decision was not part of the relation. lowering_check.mjs case 'out-of-fragment-refused' asserts decided true, implemented false, three DECLARED falsifiers, and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID distinct from LOWERING_SEM_ID; 9/9 with the refinement witness unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. THE THREE FALSIFIERS ARE DECLARED AND NONE IS WRITTEN -- I-4a allocation-invariance, I-4b source-name-sensitivity, I-4c binding-has-force -- so this law is PROPERTY-TESTED for the DECISION and its refusal surface, and carries NO claim about instantiation behaviour, which does not exist yet. B2 writes the three. B1.1: lowering_check.mjs case 'semantic-ids-track-semantics-only' asserts that no lifecycle field appears in either semantic projection AND that the projections remain sensitive -- dropping `add` from lowered_ops moves the LOWERING id while changing extra-input semantics or making the source name non-semantic moves the INSTANTIATION id and not lowering's, which is the two-relation ruling measured rather than asserted. Case 'extra-inputs-ignored-by-the-source' runs the real evaluator: input(x) with {x:2, y:999} returns 2, with {} raises program-input-missing. 11/11, and the refinement witness is unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. B1.2: lowering_check.mjs case 'target-template-is-the-pre-allocation-layer' shows the codomain is {t:add,a:{t:church,n:2},b:{t:church,n:3}} with no names and no labels, that emit() reproduces the SAME 129 characters of ic32 the pre-template lowering produced -- so introducing the layer changed neither the executable term nor its outcome -- that a template holding a port is emit-unbound-port rather than emitted, and that structural equality is identity while add(3,2) differs. 12/12, refinement unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B1.2.1 and kept as history. Revision 2 ruled that instantiation carries its own identity and then let that identity name its CODOMAIN in prose, so the executable encoding was a semantic dependency hiding behind the symbol name emit(): changing the add combinator changed the emitted term and moved no id that owns it. The separation of relations was right; the content of one of the two identities was incomplete. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED -- instantiate() has never run.
attrs.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse. CORRECTED AT B1.1, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE PART OF THE LAW. (1) A SEMANTIC IDENTITY MAY NOT HASH LIFECYCLE. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. B1 froze extra inputs as instantiate-extra-input on the reasoning that accepting them would let inputs_sem_id vary while target_term_sem_id did not, 'so the receipt would stop being a function'. A function may be many-to-one; (template, {x:2}) and (template, {x:2, unused:999}) mapping to one term IS a function. Worse, the rule contradicted the source: evaluate({op:'input',name:'x'}, {}, {x:2, y:999}) returns 2, so refusing extras at the target would have broken refinement BY CONSTRUCTION on the first program carrying a spare input. Different inputs_sem_id mapping to the same target_term_sem_id is the correct statement that executable semantics do not depend on unused data. Narrowing the source's input discipline is a SOURCE-LANGUAGE change requiring a new CORE_SEM_ID, and the instantiator may not impose it unilaterally. THE REFINEMENT CLAIM IS SCOPED BEFORE IT IS MADE: it holds over canonical, fully bound input environments in which instantiation succeeds. Missing inputs are refused on BOTH sides but at different layers under different codes -- program-input-missing during source evaluation, instantiate-missing-input before any target term exists -- so SOURCE-REFUSAL to INSTANTIATION-REFUSAL preservation is a separate theorem and is DECLARED OPEN. AND I-4c MANDATES AN ASYMMETRIC FIXTURE: add(input(x), input(y)) with x=2,y=3 gives 5 under the correct binding and 5 under the swap, so the obvious witness is green whether or not the binding was honoured. The mandated fixture is add(input(x), add(input(x), input(y))) with x=2,y=3, which gives 7 correctly and 8 swapped. COMPLETED AT B1.2, because @2 froze an architecture the compiler could not express. lower() emitted an ic32 STRING, so there was no canonical target-AST layer for {op:'input-port'} to live at and a port could only have become a placeholder like $input_x -- spelling as semantics, the very defect this law forbids, reintroduced by the absence of the representation it presumes. THE CODOMAIN OF LOWERING IS A TEMPLATE: TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, grammar church(n) | add(Template, Template) | port(source_name), with its own content-bound encoding identity. A TEMPLATE CONTAINS NO BINDER NAMES AND NO DUP LABELS -- emit() invents both from the template's shape by the declared depth-first policy -- so I-4a is a property of the DATA STRUCTURE and not a convention an emitter is asked to respect: there is no field an allocation could occupy. emit() REFUSES a template still holding a port (emit-unbound-port), because a template with a free port is not an executable term. The LoweringReceipt therefore ends at target_template_sem_id, not target_term_sem_id; a receipt ending at the term keeps asserting that lowering produced the executable term, which this law denies. AND THE HASHED SEMANTICS NOW CARRY THE WHOLE SOURCE FRAGMENT INCLUDING `input`: @2 left it out of lowered_ops, so B2 adding it would have moved LOWERING_SEM_ID -- implementing a frozen rule re-identifying the relation, which is exactly what the B1.1 correction set out to prevent. The rule is frozen ({op:'input',name:N} lowers to {t:'port',source_name:N}, N carried through unchanged) and the implementation is absent, and lower-input-not-implemented is a STATUS refusal that is deliberately NOT in refusal_semantics. Measured: implementing the input rule AND flipping both lifecycle flags moves neither semantic id.
